description: p2p.kiwi 🥝, Cross-Platform screen 🖥️ sharing 📡 made simple ⚡.

summary.one_liner: p2p.kiwi is a cross-platform peer-to-peer screen sharing and conferencing app for Mac, Windows, and Linux that requires no account.
summary.what_it_does: The README describes p2p.kiwi as a simple screen sharing tool for Mac, Windows, and Linux. It shares screens over a peer-to-peer WebRTC connection without requiring accounts. STUN and optional TURN servers are used only to exchange ICE connectivity information, and the README states it is not a signaling server for chat or media keys. It describes an E2EE design in which MLS manages group membership and application keys, and SFrame encrypts media frames, with DTLS-SRTP providing transport security. The README gives install options: a manual download from GitHub releases, an Arch Linux AUR package (p2p-kiwi-bin), and a Homebrew cask. The README contains no build or development instructions.
use_cases: share my screen with a colleague without an account
pair program remotely on one machine
screen sharing on Mac, Windows, or Linux
encrypted screen sharing for private calls
how_to_run: Download the latest release from the GitHub releases page (manual install)
notable: Peer-to-peer screen sharing with no account required
Cross-platform desktop support for Mac, Windows, and Linux
Documented E2EE design using MLS key management and SFrame media encryption
Installable via Arch AUR and Homebrew cask as well as manual download
caveats: README does not document the E2EE implementation status beyond the architecture description
Optional TURN server use may be needed for some network setups (README mentions optional TURN)
README includes no build or development instructions
keywords: share my screen with a colleague
